pr_title: scheduler: merge Reserve and Unreserve plugins
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
> Uncomment only one ` /kind <>` line, hit enter to put that in a new line, and remove leading whitespace from that line:

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Previously, separate interfaces were defined for Reserve and Unreserve
plugins. However, in nearly all cases, a plugin that allocates a
resource using Reserve will likely want to register itself for Unreserve
as well in order to free the allocated resource at the end of a failed
scheduling/binding cycle. Having separate plugins for Reserve and
Unreserve also adds unnecessary config toil. To that end, this patch
aims to merge the two plugins into a single interface called a
ReservationPlugin that requires implementing both the Reserve and
Unreserve methods.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

issue_context.title: Scheduling Framework: Merge Reserve and Unreserve
issue_context.body:
/kind cleanup

It doesn't make much sense for Reserve plugins to not have an Unreserve counterpart. Having them separate adds configuration toil.
I propose we merge them in a single interface and a single PluginSet in the configuration. However, we can only do the later in a new version of component config.

/sig scheduling

Related #83557 #83726  kubernetes-sigs/scheduler-plugins#4
comments:
sounds good, we have precedence when we moved Normalize from being a standalone plugin into an extension of Score. For this one we can move unreserve to the reserve plugin and make implementing the function mandatory.

>  However, we can only do the later in a new version of component config.

we can do that in beta in this cycle, right?
Yes, I can include the planned modifications in the KEP. Good thing is that we don't have in-tree (Un)Reserver plugins.
@adtac is interested in helping out here

One potential issue that occurred to me while implementing this is the loss of the ability to do custom ordering when unreserving things if we merge the two into a single plugin. For example, a workload with three reserve plugins A, B, C (in that order) may require the Unreserve method to be called in the reverse order. That is, C may be required to be unreserved before B is unreserved.

This is trivially possible in the current implementation -- a user can explicitly define the order in which plugins should be run. However, a single plugin will no longer allow them to do this.

One potential real use case for something like this is nested mountpoints. If B mounts a directory inside a directory mounted by A, then B must usually be unmounted before A is unmounted.

I'm not sure if scheduler plugins are required to be independent of each other, but if we make this a requirement, we will no longer have this problem (also has potential side-benefits such as running multiple plugins concurrently).

Another solution would be execute Unreserve operations in the reverse order of Reserve operations. This makes sense from a logical standpoint -- unreserve reverses all the reserve operations. If plugins are truly independent of each other, the reverse order shouldn't matter; but if they are dependent, reverse order makes the most sense. However, I feel that this inconsistency in ordering might be confusing to some users.

Any thoughts?

The intention is for Reserve/UnReserve to act as "assume" and "cancel-assume", so they are informational [1]. Doing the actual binding of resources should happen in PreBind, just like our VolumeBinding plugin does [2]

The other thing is that plugins should be independent of each other, so order shouldn't matter. However, one thing we should expect from Unreserve calls is for them to be idempotent.

@mrkm4ntr @cofyc Do you foresee any problems with ordering of UnReserve calls?

[1](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-scheduling/20180409-scheduling-framework.md#reserve)
[2](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/13f1d956ea2741be4c11e90340ed1c4e0b515a8c/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding/volume_binding.go#L189)
I think calling in reverse order makes sense with proper documentation it should be fine.
I don't foresee any problems.  Reverse order seems to be fine.
Thanks guys! Let's proceed with that.

review_comments: nit: `an error ocurred during reservation of subsequent plugins` doesn't apply in this PR.

Isn't v1beta1 a live type? You can't remove this field.

I think you can instead add validation that requires it to either be empty or the same as the reserve list, ignore it everywhere else, and then remove it in the next version.
It's not. v1alpha2 was in 1.18. v1beta1 is being introduced now #89701
ah ok sorry. I can't keep track of what is where.

Here we should call Unreserve #83557

We will need a test for it.
I'd like to implement the merge of the two plugins first and then handle the case of failing reserves later in a separate PR to keep this PR small, atomic, and contained to one issue.
Could I recreate https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/83557 after this PR will be merged?
@adtac could take it, since he is already modifying the code here. Unless you @mrkm4ntr  have some specific need?
I'd like to see this feature to completion, but if you'd strongly like to work on that feature after this PR, I don't mind :)
Oh, I misunderstood. I have nothing to do :)
